policy.title: AI Acceptable Use Policy
policy.review: Every 6 months, or when a tool or rule changes

sections.title: Why this policy exists
items: AI tools help us work faster. This policy tells you which tools to use, what data can go into them, and what stays human.
It applies to everyone who works for us, on any device, whenever company or customer information is involved.

sections.title: Five principles
items: AI helps; people decide.
Protect data: only put in what the tool is approved for.
You own the output: check it before you use it.
Be open about AI use when it matters to the reader.
Speak up when something looks wrong.

sections.title: Data: what can go where
items: Every piece of information has a class: Public, Internal, Confidential or Restricted.
Use a tool only for data up to the class it's approved for (see the table).
Restricted data goes only into a tool approved for that exact data and task. Today that's Support Copilot, for customer data in support work.
Never put passwords, keys, tokens, payment card numbers, bank account numbers or government ID numbers into any AI tool.

sections.title: Tools
items: Use the approved tools first. They run on our enterprise accounts and don't train on our data.
Blocked tools (for example NoteHawk and TabGenie AI) must not be used, even if a customer or supplier invites them.
Public chatbots with personal accounts: published content only, never signed in with a company email.
Need a tool that isn't listed? Request it through AI vendor intake. Don't start with a free trial.

sections.title: Never use AI to
items: Make or recommend decisions about people: hiring, firing, pay, promotion or discipline.
Imitate a real person's voice, face or writing without their written consent.
Get around security controls, monitoring or this policy.
Monitor or profile colleagues.

sections.title: Your responsibilities
items: A person reviews anything AI drafts before it reaches a customer.
Check facts, figures, code and sources. AI output is your work once you use it.
Tell everyone in a meeting before AI takes notes, and delete recordings within 30 days.
Label AI-generated images and media in external content.

sections.title: Speak up
items: If you see AI used against this policy, talk to the person, ask the AI help desk, or report it. Anonymous reports are welcome.
Reports start with coaching, not discipline. Retaliation against anyone who speaks up is not allowed.
Never forward or screenshot the sensitive data itself when you report.

sections.title: Exceptions
items: Ask the AI Governance Committee for an exception with a business reason, an owner and an end date. Wait for approval before you start.

history.change: Added Support Copilot for customer data; added the five principles.
Blocked NoteHawk and TabGenie AI (blacklist v3.2); added 4.2 and 6.3.
